value.statement: LR.Strings l (rho x) (rho y) (rho h) v
value.explanation: Unpack the representation and Chevalley commutator laws; induct simultaneously on the natural exponent. H001 identifies nonnegative integer exponents with naturals.

value.statement: (∀ i : LR.I l, LR.eNat (rho y) v i.val ≠ 0) ∧ LinearIndependent ℂ (fun i : LR.I l => LR.eNat (rho y) v i.val)
value.explanation: Apply repeated raising to prove nonvanishing. Isolate each coefficient by the product of h minus the other complex weights; cancel the nonzero weight differences. Do not use distinctness in characteristic p.

value.statement: LR.BasisString l (rho y) v
value.explanation: Use the independent family of size finrank to construct the basis. Expand the next lowering vector, compare its weight with every basis weight, and deduce termination and all higher vanishings.

value.statement: LR.Matrices l (rho x) (rho y) (rho h) (LR.eNat (rho y) v)
value.explanation: Divide the string formulas by complex factorials, retaining the endpoint zero cases.

value.statement: LR.N1 l (rho x) (rho y) (rho h) v
value.explanation: Iterate the matrices to derive both divided-power formulas and zero cases, using Nat.choose and its factorial identity under the displayed natural bounds. Assemble N001 including the basis, strings, termination, cardinality and integer coefficients.

value.statement: LR.LocalRingSpec p ∧ ∃ (m : Module.Basis (LR.I l) ℤ M) (bc : Module.Basis (LR.I l) ℂ V), ∀ i, (m i : V) = bc i
value.explanation: Prove that the explicit fraction set is a subring, so its closure is exactly itself, and prove the unit criterion. Reindex a simultaneous lattice/complex basis by I using finite-dimensionality and cardinality; use the library's strong rank condition for the field.

value.statement: Nonempty (LR.Action K M rho x y h) ∧ ∃ f : LR.MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V, LR.IotaSpec p M f ∧ LR.LocalBasis p l M f ∧ LR.Preserved p M f (rho x) (rho y)
value.explanation: Base-change the simultaneous integer basis to R; construct the pure-tensor embedding and prove injectivity through complex independence. Extend lattice operators to the scalar extension, prove bracket closure of the integer span, and construct the induced K-linear action with its pure-tensor commutator law.

value.statement: LR.SmallUnits p l
value.explanation: Apply the pinned factorial divisibility theorem at r≤l.toNat<p. Use the exact R fraction characterization to invert factorials and each binomial coefficient.

value.statement: ∀ b : Module.Basis (LR.I l) ℂ V, LR.BasisSpec l (rho y) v b → LR.UnitIdentities l (rho x) (rho y) b
value.explanation: Check the three operator identities on every basis vector using the existing divided-power formulas; Fin.last l.toNat represents the source index λ.

value.statement: LR.N2 p l K M rho x y h v
value.explanation: Combine the three identities and invert the binomial scalar to obtain each matrix unit. Closure under composition and R-scalars proves preservation of the embedded arbitrary lattice. Bundle all N002 clauses without assuming an embedding or action in advance.

value.statement: ∀ (r : LR.R p) (c : LR.C p), LR.cv p (r • c) = (((r : ℚ) : ℂ)) * LR.cv p c
value.explanation: Checked representation bridge for the restriction-of-scalars wrapper: use the pinned RestrictScalars.smul_def and the subtype algebra map R→ℚ followed by the rational embedding ℚ→ℂ. cv is the supplied additive equivalence, so zero, sums and bijectivity already hold.

value.statement: ∀ f : LR.MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V, LR.IotaSpec p M f → ∃ J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p), LR.CoeffSpec p l (rho y) v M f J
value.explanation: The pure-tensor specification makes f the unique canonical embedding. Matrix units identify all coordinate modules with J0; projected finite basis coordinates generate J. Prove it nonzero and build the coordinate R-linear equivalence. cv makes the restriction-of-scalars identification explicit.

value.statement: ∀ J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p), J.FG → LR.RationalEmbedding p J
value.explanation: Tensor a finite generating set to prove finite-dimensionality. Construct μ by multiplication; put any finite tensor sum over a common nonzero integer denominator to prove injectivity. Its range is exactly the rational span.

value.statement: Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] LR.MR p M) = l.toNat+1
value.explanation: Choose the R-basis exported by N002 and apply Basis.baseChange over ℚ, then finrank_eq_card_basis. No M premise port is required.

value.statement: ∀ (f : LR.MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p)), LR.IotaSpec p M f → LR.CoeffSpec p l (rho y) v M f J → Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] J) = 1
value.explanation: Tensor the coordinate equivalence with ℚ. Construct inverse coordinate maps to identify the result with I→(ℚ⊗R J). Use finite-dimensional product finrank to get n=n*r and cancel positive n.

value.statement: ∀ J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p), LR.RationalEmbedding p J → Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] J) = 1 → LR.RationalMultiples p J
value.explanation: For any chosen nonzero a∈J, μ shows 1⊗a is nonzero. Its independent singleton spans the one-dimensional rational tensor space, so applying μ writes every element of J as a rational multiple of a.

value.statement: LR.PDecomposition p
value.explanation: Factor the nonzero integer numerator and positive denominator by powers of p. The remaining signed fraction and its inverse lie in R; package it as a unit. The integer exponent uses field zpow, allowing negative valuations.

value.statement: LR.N3 p l (rho y) v M
value.explanation: Use a finite nonempty list of nonzero generators, rational multiples of a and their p-decompositions. A minimum valuation produces b and J=Rb. Prove the scaled basis property for every such nonzero generator; bundle the coordinate decomposition, μ and rational rank as N003.

value.statement: Nonempty (LR.Residue p K)
value.explanation: Construct the maps R→K and R→ZMod p by the fraction formula; prove compatibility with the prime-field map, surjectivity, kernel pR and the quotient ring equivalence, and that units have nonzero images.

value.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.Bridge p K M Q
value.explanation: Construct Γ and Δ with their specified inverses by tensor/quotient universal properties. ModN is the actual quotient by p multiples with its canonical ZMod action. Check formulas on pure tensors and prove commutation with arbitrary induced lattice and R-linear operators.

value.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.Transfer p l K M (rho y) v Q
value.explanation: For every specified scaled R-basis, base-change to K and transport through Γ. The first-factor convention incorporates the source tensor flips. Preserve the chosen b and basis vectors, and prove the stated K-dimension.

value.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.MatrixTransport p l K M rho x y h v Q
value.explanation: For any witnesses satisfying the exact embedding and Γ formulas, transport integer action matrices and all divided-power matrices. The integer coefficients commute with the ring maps; injectivity of f identifies the required lattice vectors. Construct the reduced operators from actual restrictions.

value.statement: LR.SmallPowers l K M rho x y h
value.explanation: Tensor the characteristic-zero identities r!X(r)=x^r and r!Y(r)=y^r. Their restrictions exist by N002; the residue/unit facts make r! nonzero for r≤λ, so cancellation yields the two reduced divided powers.

value.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.PolynomialTransport p l K M rho x y h v Q
value.explanation: Extend the already proved localized matrix-unit identity through Γ, using equality on pure tensors and preservation of compositions. Substitute the small divided-power equalities to obtain the exact polynomial and its coordinate action. All indices λ−i, λ, λ−j satisfy the small-power guard.

value.statement: LR.N4 p l K M rho x y h v
value.explanation: Assemble N004: choose residue data, canonical f, coefficient module J and a nonzero cyclic generator from N003, then a scaled R-basis and its transported K-basis. Keep these same witnesses for all matrices and formulas. Export both tensor identifications, the positive dimension, and every reduced matrix-unit clause.

value.statement: ∀ (A : LR.Action K M rho x y h) (W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M)), LR.Stable W A.a → LR.Stable W A.d → ∀ i j : LR.I l, LR.Stable W (LR.polynomial l A.a A.d i j)
value.explanation: Finite induction proves that invariant subspaces are stable under all nonnegative powers, their compositions and K-scalar multiples. Apply this to the displayed polynomial.

value.statement: ∀ (beta : Module.Basis (LR.I l) K (LR.VK K M)) (W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M)), W ≠ ⊥ → ∃ (w : LR.VK K M) (c : LR.I l → K) (j : LR.I l), w ∈ W ∧ w ≠ 0 ∧ w = ∑ i, c i • beta i ∧ c j ≠ 0
value.explanation: Choose a nonzero vector of the nonzero subspace, expand it in the finite basis and select a nonzero coefficient. Close all witnesses inside the existential statement.

value.statement: ∀ (A : LR.Action K M rho x y h) (beta : Module.Basis (LR.I l) K (LR.VK K M)) (W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M)), (∀ i j k : LR.I l, LR.polynomial l A.a A.d i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0) → (∀ i j : LR.I l, LR.Stable W (LR.polynomial l A.a A.d i j)) → W ≠ ⊥ → W = ⊤
value.explanation: Use the same w,c,j witnesses. Each matrix unit sends w to c_j beta_i; cancel the nonzero scalar in K, then use spanning of the basis.

value.statement: LR.Target K M rho x y h
value.explanation: Choose the induced action from N002 and the basis exported by N004. Its positive cardinality proves nontriviality. For every invariant subspace use the zero case or T027. The integer span's scalar extension has the same invariant subspaces as its three generators; no reduced weight separation or algebraic closure is used.

patches.value: Use the actual complex Lie algebra LR.L=LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ, the subtype of trace-zero 2×2 matrices with commutator bracket (pinned Classical.lean:94–99). x,y,h remain arbitrary Chevalley generators: H002 explicitly records IsSl2Triple h x y, their complex linear span being all of LR.L, the Lie representation law, finite dimension λ+1, irreducibility and existence of a primitive highest-weight vector. The pinned IsSl2Triple declaration includes h≠0 and exactly [x,y]=h, [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, where 2• is natural repeated addition. A linear rho plus its explicit H002 commutator law is the usual Lie representation, avoiding an implicit theorem in a typeclass. H003 retains the chosen nonzero highest-weight vector. H001 keeps primality, CharP, nonnegativity and the strict λ

P.explanation: The assembled theorem universally quantifies the displayed p:ℕ, λ:ℤ, arbitrary field K, complex module V/rho, Chevalley generators x,y,h, highest-weight v and arbitrary additive lattice M, under exactly H001–H004. Field/AddCommGroup/Module parameters are ambient structures; primality, CharP K p, 0≤λ<p, finite dimension, irreducibility, highest-weight conditions, simultaneous lattice bases and admissibility remain explicit premises. The traceless 2×2 complex matrix realization presents the original sl₂(ℂ); a Chevalley triple and its span state the source Chevalley-generator convention. The primitive-vector clause is the highest-weight condition relative to x,h. H004 preservation of all divided powers is equivalent in both directions to U_Z-stability by induction on the generated integer algebra. Fin indexing is the exact interval using λ≥0. VK=K⊗ℤM is identified with M⊗ℤK by flipping factors, preserving its scalar action. Target says VK is nontrivial and produces its actual induced Action together with ∀ K-linear subspaces W, stability under its three generator operators implies W=⊥ or W=⊤. Action is not an additional premise: its existence is proved in N002 from lattice preservation. Its pure-tensor formulas uniquely determine the full action and all three operators, so an existential Action carrying this universal invariant-subspace assertion implies the assertion for the originally defined action, and conversely the original assertion plus its constructed action gives Target. Nontrivial means existence of two different vectors, equivalently VK≠0. Bottom/top submodules are zero/all. Bilinearity and the integer span show that the three-generator invariant subspaces are exactly LK-submodules. This retains the entire original target, λ=0 and p=2, with arbitrary K and no distinctness of reduced weights; the claimed correspondences remain for independent semantic review.
